sections.h2: Which county bills me for property tax in Atlanta?
sections.html:
Fulton County bills most of the city, but Atlanta also extends into DeKalb County, so check which county your parcel sits in before you call anyone. Atlanta is the county seat of Fulton and spreads across the Fulton and DeKalb line, which means two assessors and two tax commissioners are involved citywide.

For Fulton parcels, the Board of Assessors sets the value and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner bills and collects for Fulton County, Fulton County and City of Atlanta Schools, the State of Georgia, and the City of Atlanta. Fulton has 18 taxing jurisdictions in all, each setting its own rate, and each is listed separately on the bill. For DeKalb parcels, the DeKalb Property Appraisal Department sets values, and its resource page gives the same 40 percent assessment ratio and a 45-day appeal window from the notice date.

  • Fulton Board of Assessors: 404-612-6440
  • Fulton Tax Commissioner: 404-613-6100, 141 Pryor Street SW
  • DeKalb Property Appraisal: 404-371-0841

sections.h2: When were Atlanta property taxes due in 2026?
sections.html:
City of Atlanta taxes were due September 30, 2026, and Fulton County taxes and those from all other jurisdictions were due October 15, 2026. Both dates have passed, and unpaid 2026 balances accrue interest.

2026 Fulton County property tax calendar (source: Fulton County press releases, June to August 2026)
EventDate
Assessment notices available onlineJune 19, 2026
Appeal deadline for most ownersJuly 31, 2026
Tax bills mailedAugust 15, 2026
City of Atlanta taxes dueSeptember 30, 2026
Fulton County and other jurisdictions dueOctober 15, 2026

Fulton's 2026 bills were temporary. A delay in sending the tax digest to the state meant the Superior Court of Fulton County authorized, on August 4, 2026, bills built on the preliminary 2026 digest and each jurisdiction's 2025 millage rate. Final rates are set once the state certifies the digest, and a refund or revised bill goes out only if needed.

Interest begins the day after the due date. An extra 5 percent penalty is added on the 120th day, and another 5 percent every 120 days after that, up to a maximum of 20 percent. The office accepts partial payments, though interest keeps accruing on the unpaid principal.

sections.h2: How do I pay an Atlanta property tax bill?
sections.html:
Pay online at fultoncountytaxes.org, by phone at 404-613-6100, by mail, or in person at the Tax Commissioner's office in the Fulton County Government Center, 141 Pryor Street SW. The office also operates three other full-service locations.

Mail goes to the Fulton County Tax Commissioner, 141 Pryor St. SW, Suite 1106, Atlanta, GA 30303. The office's website lets you search for a bill by parcel ID, account number or address, and it supports a multi-parcel summary lookup for owners with several properties. Credit card and e-check payments run through the same system. If an expected bill has not arrived by mid-September in a billing year, Fulton asks owners to call rather than wait.

Escrow does not remove the owner's responsibility. If your lender pays the tax, still confirm that the payment posted against the right parcel, particularly after a refinance or a servicer change.

sections.h2: What do I need to know about Atlanta's size, neighborhoods and housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate counts 529,110 residents across about 135 square miles of land, at an elevation near 1,050 feet. Owners are a minority: 46.4 percent of the 236,468 households own, per the 2020 to 2024 survey.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $439,600 and the middle monthly rent is $1,711. The city counts 242 officially defined neighborhoods. Three high-rise districts, Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead, run north to south along Peachtree, and most of the land between them is low-density single-family housing with a craftsman bungalow common in older areas.

  • Three interstates meet here: I-20, I-75 and I-85, with the Downtown Connector carrying more than 340,000 vehicles a day and I-285 mostly encircling the city as the Perimeter.
  • MARTA rail connects the airport, Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead.
  • Georgia Tech, Georgia State, Emory and the Atlanta University Center are among more than 15 colleges and universities in the city.
  • Atlanta annexed Emory into the city effective January 1, 2018.

Atlanta has a humid subtropical climate with about 50 inches of rain a year spread evenly through the seasons, and it is often called the City in a Forest for the density of its tree canopy. Older bungalow streets inside the Perimeter and newer construction beyond it can sit in the same assessment cycle but under different taxing jurisdictions, which is why a street-level look at your own bill matters.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Atlanta assessment in Fulton County?
sections.html:
File within 45 days of the date on your Notice of Assessment, online at fultonassessor.org, in person at a Board of Assessors office, or by mail. For 2026, notices went out in June and the deadline for most owners was July 31, 2026, unless another date was printed on the notice.

The appeal covers the assessed value only, and the estimated tax cannot be appealed. Each appeal must pick one of three paths: a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on valuation, or a hearing officer, and the last two can carry fees. Hearings are held at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 2111, and the Board of Equalization office takes scheduling calls at 404-613-7792. Useful evidence includes the purchase price, an appraisal, photographs and comparable sales.

Either side can carry a Board of Equalization decision to Superior Court within 30 days of its mailing date. The appeals process can run for months, and Fulton warns that a temporary bill issued while an appeal is pending must still be paid or penalties apply. The 2026 notices also carried a new format under Senate Bill 566, with an Estimated Tax Savings section replacing the old estimated tax table.

  • Board of Assessors, Fulton County Center: 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018
  • Customer Service Center: 11575 Maxwell Road
  • North Fulton Customer Service Center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210
  • South Fulton Service Center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, Suite 224

All four are reached through the same assessor line, 404-612-6440.

sections.h2: What if I sell an Atlanta house while taxes are unpaid?
sections.html:
Plan to clear the balance through the closing, since unpaid Atlanta and Fulton tax follows the parcel. Georgia assigns a year's bill to whoever owned the home on January 1, and the state revenue department says there is no refund for a partial year if you sell and move.

Ask the Fulton Tax Commissioner for a payoff total that includes interest and any 5 percent penalty steps. The temporary billing used in 2026 adds one wrinkle: because a corrected bill or refund may follow once final rates are set, the closing attorney should agree in the contract how any later adjustment between buyer and seller will be handled.

A buyer's exemption starts fresh. Fulton's assessment announcement says owners who held the home on January 1 and missed the April 1 homestead deadline can still apply during the appeal period, while owners who bought after January 1 apply for the following tax year.

faqs.q: Were Atlanta property tax bills final in 2026?
faqs.a: No. Fulton County issued temporary bills based on the preliminary 2026 digest and 2025 millage rates, as authorized by the Superior Court on August 4, 2026. A revised bill or refund follows only after final rates are set.

faqs.q: Is part of Atlanta in DeKalb County?
faqs.a: Yes. Atlanta is the seat of Fulton County and extends into DeKalb County. Parcels in the DeKalb part are valued by DeKalb Property Appraisal rather than the Fulton Board of Assessors, so confirm the county on your bill.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal in Fulton County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the Notice of Assessment. For most 2026 notices that ended July 31, 2026. After the deadline passes the right to appeal that year's value is lost.

faqs.q: How is a late Atlanta tax bill penalized?
faqs.a: Interest starts the day after the due date. A 5 percent penalty is added on the 120th day and again every 120 days, up to 20 percent total. Fulton accepts partial payments, but interest continues on what remains unpaid.

faqs.q: Which office do I call about my Atlanta home value?
faqs.a: For a Fulton County parcel, call the Board of Assessors at 404-612-6440. For billing or payment questions, call the Fulton Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100. DeKalb parcels go to DeKalb Property Appraisal at 404-371-0841.
